solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: How disgusting, cheese sandwiches — what players'll get through quickly

indicators.note: a sandwich has its filling held between two slices, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: FETTA is a variant spelling of feta, the Greek cheese
an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at a cheese that is wedged between two layers of something.
explanation.walkthrough: FETTA is an accepted variant spelling of feta. The definition is cryptic: musicians get through a short fugue quickly because it is brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A fughetta is a short fugue, a piece of music that performers finish in little time.

clue.text: Batch of terrific tiles, or descriptive thereof?

indicators.note: a batch is a portion of a larger lot, so the letters are a run taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the run of letters across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A load of marvellous tiles, or a word that would describe them.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across terriFIC TILEs, and it is also the adjective that describes those very tiles, which is why the clue ends with a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Fictile means moulded from clay, as pottery is, so it is the right adjective for fired tiles.

clue.text: One has to admit former match revolting

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the first word takes the next one inside it

parts.note: 'un is the dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
prise is an obsolete word for a contest or match

explanation.surface: Someone must confess that an old fixture was a disgusting affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'disgusting', but here it means rising in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisen means having risen up, so it describes people in rebellion, the sense of revolting here.

clue.text: Clot using recipe that slices seed pod the French avoided

indicators.note: something that slices cuts into the middle, so it sits within the other piece
what is avoided is left out, so those letters come away from the word

parts.note: a legume is a pod such as a pea's
LE is French for the
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on a prescription

explanation.surface: An idiot follows a recipe in which pods are cut up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a fool, but it is a clotted lump. R for recipe comes from the Latin 'take' heading a prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: Grume is a thick, viscous fluid or a clot of blood, so it matches clot as a noun for a lump.

clue.text: Rob crinkly going after inexpert banker

indicators.note: something crinkly is crumpled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ham means clumsy or amateurish
the three letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly thief follows a bungling banker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after' puts the rearranged word after HAM. 'Crinkly' is slang for an old person, which hides its role.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hambros are a London merchant banking family, so a Hambro is a member of that banking dynasty.

clue.text: 'Fiddlesticks!' I yell wildly in middle of telly passage

indicators.note: doing something wildly means doing it in disorder, so those letters are jumbled
placed in the middle of another word means sitting inside it

parts.note: TV is the abbreviation for television, the telly
the letters rearranged
an alley is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: Someone shouts an exasperated 'Fiddlesticks!' during a passage of a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Telly is British slang for television, and its middle is the gap between the two letters of its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilley-valley is an old exclamation of impatience, found in Shakespeare, meaning nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Assist court somehow with little latitude in cheapest seats? (12, two words)

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together in another order

parts.note: the letters as written
L is the abbreviation for latitude, little because cut short

explanation.surface: Someone is told to help hold court despite being cramped in the cheap seats.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra L comes from 'little latitude', and the phrase also describes the cramped seating, which is why the clue ends in a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourist class is the cheapest class of travel on an aircraft or ship, with the least legroom.

clue.text: Soak newspaper up in a flash?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax to soften it
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone soaks up a newspaper very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: RETRAG read upwards gives GARTER. 'In a flash' is not about speed: flashes are the coloured tabs attached to the garters of kilt stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Garter flashes are ribbon tabs worn on kilt hose, so a garter is what is found in a flash.

clue.text: Plough's components I brought into the market-place with spades

indicators.note: bringing something into a place puts it inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: trone, or tron, is a Scots word for a market-place with a public weighing beam
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A farmer brings plough parts and spades to the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plough here is the constellation, not farm equipment. I goes into TRONE, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Triones are the seven stars of the Plough, the Great Bear, from Latin for plough oxen.

clue.text: Supporter tense, formerly lively (in happier times)

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the bracketed words, as a second route

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a bonus: the same letters run across the join of these words, a second route to the same answer

explanation.surface: A tense supporter who was cheerful in better days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' marks the word as obsolete. As a bonus, the answer also sits inside 'hapPIER Times', confirming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Piert is an old word, a variant of peart, meaning brisk, cheerful and in good spirits.

clue.text: Top club boat's bumped

indicators.note: something bumped is knocked about, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the letters as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The leading rowing club's boat has been bumped in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumping is a style of rowing race at Oxford and Cambridge, but here it shuffles the letters. 'Top club' is a playing card, not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card games ombre and quadrille, basto is the ace of clubs, the top-ranking trump.

clue.text: Air after old air trilled — they're primitive in the main

indicators.note: a trill makes notes flutter back and forth, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: an aria is an air, a song in an opera
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer warbles one tune after an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the sea, which is where these primitive creatures live.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiolaria are single-celled marine protozoa with silica skeletons, ancient and simple organisms of the ocean.

clue.text: Egg going off? See bit left

indicators.note: the spoken word is matched by a letter of the alphabet that is pronounced the same

parts.note: the letter name is pronounced like the word
a rump is a remnant, the part left over

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs an egg that may have gone bad and notices a scrap remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' is old RAF slang for a bomb, so 'going off' means exploding, not rotting.
explanation.definitionFit: A crump is the dull bang of a bursting shell or bomb, the sound of one exploding.

clue.text: Sign most circumspect should shed weight externally

indicators.note: to shed something is to drop it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: wariest means most cautious

indicators.note: the outside of a word means its first and last letters only

parts.note: the outside letters of this word

explanation.surface: A sign that the most cautious people ought to lose some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: WARIEST drops its W and T, its own outer letters, which match the outside of 'weight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Drum providing most of rhythm accompanying Parisian dance

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter

parts.note: time, in the musical sense of rhythm, without its final letter
bal is French for a dance or ball

explanation.surface: A drum beats out the rhythm for a dance in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accompanying' just places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbal, or tymbal, is a kettledrum.

clue.text: Comeback achieved when hare meets tortoise?

indicators.note: where two words meet, the tail of one runs straight into the head of the other

parts.note: the end of this word
the start of this word

explanation.surface: A reference to the fable of the hare and the tortoise, as though the slow animal made a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the two animals side by side: where hare meets tortoise the letters read haRE TORToise.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, a verbal comeback.

clue.text: Exhibition's opening section arranged period of Italian art

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order
an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: its first letter
the letters as written

explanation.surface: The first room of a gallery show is laid out to cover one era of Italian painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The seicento is the seventeenth century in Italian art and literature, from Italian for six hundred.

clue.text: Sour, me? Only when out of sorts

indicators.note: out of sorts suggests being disordered, so the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are sour, and admits it is only when they feel unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemony means tasting of lemon, sharp and acid, and in slang also irritable.

clue.text: Marshy Scottish waterway penetrated by steamer

indicators.note: penetrated means entered, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: the Moray Firth is an inlet of the sea in north-east Scotland
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A steamship forces its way into a boggy Scottish inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Morassy means like a morass, boggy and wet, so it is a synonym for marshy.

clue.text: Salad plant local girl removed from Trojan mountain?

indicators.note: taking something away leaves the rest, so the one name is cut from the other

parts.note: Cressida is the Trojan heroine of Troilus and Cressida, a girl local to Troy
Mount Ida stands near Troy

explanation.surface: A girl from the district is picking salad on a mountain near Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl and the mountain share their ending: take IDA off CRESSIDA and the salad plant is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a small peppery plant eaten raw in salads and sandwiches.

clue.text: We're allowed occasional solos — pity when township's involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up within, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: sin can mean a shame or pity, as in 'it's a sin'
a deme is a township of ancient Attica

explanation.surface: Band players complain it is a shame when the town gets mixed up in their occasional solos.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the musicians speaking for themselves: backing players who get the odd solo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidemen are supporting members of a band, mainly accompanying the leader but given an occasional solo.

clue.text: Band rocking in saucy stuff? He'll be happy

indicators.note: rocking means moving to and fro, so the letters are shaken into a new order
one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: soy is a sauce
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock band playing amid risqué material will be cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like cheeky; here it means literally a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'happy as a sandboy' means perfectly content, so a sandboy is proverbially happy.

clue.text: What's that about prisoner returning in Arden?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: eh is said when asking someone to repeat themselves

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a con is a convict

explanation.surface: Someone queries a convict coming back to the Forest of Arden.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden suggests Shakespeare's forest, but the answer is part of the name of Tennyson's poem Enoch Arden.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch Arden is the title character of Tennyson's poem, so his first name is what is found with Arden.

clue.text: Courtesy? Neglect replaces it in e.g. London

indicators.note: replacing means putting one thing in another's place in the word

parts.note: London is an example of a city
the two letters to be swapped out
to omit is to neglect or leave out

explanation.surface: Is politeness neglected in a big city like London?
explanation.walkthrough: In CITY, the letters IT are swapped for OMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Comity means courtesy and civility, as in the comity of nations.

clue.text: Decorative inlay — mass taken from Asian land formerly by sailor

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes that letter from it

parts.note: Siam is the former name of Thailand
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A sailor brings home ornate inlaid woodwork from the old kingdom of Thailand, minus some bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By sailor' puts TAR beside the shortened country, and here it goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsia is Italian inlaid woodwork, the decorative technique also called intarsia.

clue.text: Impoverished descendant of settlers, one that altered given lift

indicators.note: in a down entry, being lifted means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to alter an animal is to castrate it, which a gelder does

explanation.surface: A poor colonist's descendant who changed things and was given a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' is the euphemism for neutering an animal. A redleg is a poor white of Barbados descended from early settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Redleg is a Caribbean term for poor white Barbadians descended from early colonial settlers and indentured workers.

clue.text: Right leg trapped in train? That sounds very sad

indicators.note: something trapped in another thing is held inside it

parts.note: to coach is to train
R is the abbreviation for right
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Someone's right leg is caught in a railway carriage, which is a sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train but is the verb, coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronach is a Highland funeral lament or dirge, a mournful song.

clue.text: Monkey in Church coach?

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A monkey seen aboard a church outing's coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Cebus is the genus of capuchin monkeys of Central and South America.

clue.text: None in the wars died erect (5, two words)

indicators.note: being in the wars means battered about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters rearranged
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Nobody who was hurt died standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: On end means upright, standing vertically, which is what erect means.

clue.text: Dodge upcoming timetable missing school

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top
missing means lacking, so the letters for the second piece are dropped

parts.note: a schedule is a timetable
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A pupil dodges the timetable for the next term by skipping school.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or escape, so it is a synonym for dodge as a verb.

clue.text: Wing tips famous for a sort of sheen?

indicators.note: the two letters become the tips, placed at either end of the next piece

parts.note: an el is a wing or extension of a building at right angles
name as an adjective means well known, as in a name brand

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether famous wingtips are known for a particular glossy finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing tips' look like the ends of a wing or a type of shoe; here the wing word forms the ends of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard glossy coating, so it gives a surface a sheen of its own kind.

clue.text: Describing workhouse helpings, young Oliver maybe took initiative?

parts.note: Oliver Twist is an example of a young lad
to take the initiative is to lead

explanation.surface: Young Oliver Twist boldly asked for more of the workhouse gruel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Oliver Twist the orphan, in a workhouse, bravely asks for a second helping of gruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Workhouse gruel was served with a ladle, so the helpings were ladled out.

clue.text: I'll appear in No. 1 suit, as before

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be found inside it, so the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: number one means the best
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone promises to turn up in their finest suit, as on previous occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing but is a verb, and 'as before' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Besit is an archaic verb meaning to befit or become, so it matches suit in that sense.

clue.text: Fix pipes etc made of lead round Scottish chimney

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
lum is Scots for a chimney

explanation.surface: A plumber fits lead piping around a chimney in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The word derives from Latin plumbum, lead, the old material of water pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to install or repair water pipes and fittings, the work of a plumber.

clue.text: Sun idly, end of meal over, without a care

indicators.note: turned over means read backwards
letters arranged idly are put down any old way, out of their order

parts.note: the letters rearranged
dessert is the last course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone lazes in the sun after a meal, completely relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of meal' tempts you to take the last letter, L, but it is the whole course that ends a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstressed means free of strain or worry, so it describes someone without a care.

clue.text: Part of phage's development? This one may be rendered as e.g. yes/no only

indicators.note: rendering something as another thing reworks it, so these letters are reshaped into the following ones

parts.note: the letters as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a biological process that reduces to a simple yes or no.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus ONE ('This one') has the same letters as 'e.g. yes no only', so remove ONE from those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysogeny is the phase in which a bacteriophage's genome lies dormant inside its bacterial host, one stage of the virus's life cycle.
